summary: Added the missing datetime import that crashed every admin page rendering a timestamp, and argued for keeping the except clause narrow rather than widening it to swallow the next NameError; 19 passed and the sabotage reproduced the user's exact error.
Drafted the upstream issue about the Bash/PowerShell guard inconsistency into the working tree per the human's decision; verified present, all four elements found, and confirmed NOT posted.

Added the missing allowlist guard to check_url_updates before its unbounded network path, with 2 new tests - but the agent proved, and I confirmed, that this is NOT the tool issue #17 names, so the issue stays open and a re-scoping task was opened.

Bounded the embeddings load behind a deadline on a named warm-up thread after re-measuring that faiss, numpy AND sentence_transformers all stall under a pending stdin read; 58 passed, and the agent caught its own broken harness when the known-positive control failed to stall.

Root-caused the long-lived-stdio search hang to Windows serialising I/O on the stdin file object - a BLAS-linked import inside nltk blocks until a client message completes the transport's pending read - refuting both candidates the plan named, and bounded it with a deadline; 34 passed and I reproduced the mechanism independently.

SUPERSEDES the earlier record: the cause is not process death but a heavyweight lazy nltk/scipy import inside the unlogged window in search(), proven by a stack dump of a live blocked process and by a cancellation that produced no completion line.

Replaced Mount('/mcp') with two explicit Routes over an ASGI class instance so the bare path serves 200 instead of 307-redirecting; 31 passed and restoring the Mount reproduced the exact reported redirect.
Passed version=__version__ into the Server(...) construction so clients are told the project's version instead of the MCP SDK's; 32 passed and dropping the argument again made the new case fail.

Root-caused the cascade to an undrained stderr pipe in the test harness itself - not a product defect - fixed it, and the suite now passes skip-by-default with the assertion intact; the full repo is green at 412 passed / 4 skipped for the first time, and a real scrape_url hang was found and left in scope for whoever can touch util.py.

Replaced the raw PRAGMA data_version gate with a corpus fingerprint over documents and chunks, so a peer's telemetry write no longer drops the chunk cache, the BM25 index and every search cache; 13 passed, both sabotages discriminated, and an existing test caught a real ABA hole in the first design.

Bounded tool dispatch with an opt-out default plus a separate lock-wait bound, after measuring that the 'one hang kills the server' half is HTTP-only and stdio was already concurrent; 37 passed and the sabotage failed on a deadline rather than hanging.
